audit.whatIsWrong: Labelled EVEN at 6/10 while the win rate is 44.06% over 143 games. The chart already gives Kled 4 stages to Trundle's zero, and the prose says outright that 'levels 2 through 5 are Kled's lane'.
audit.why: 44.06% is a hard lane. The chart and prose already describe it that way; only the difficulty labels lag.
audit.corrected: diff to HARD, tone to the hard colour, 6/10 to 7/10 in diffRating, breakdown.difficulty and the final rating line.

audit.whatIsWrong: Bear Trap on a Rope is named as the matchup-defining ability eight times without a cooldown, and Chaaaaaaaarge!!! is described as a level-6 spike with no duration either.
audit.why: Bear Trap on a Rope is 11/10/9/8/7s, Violent Tendencies and Jousting are both 13/12/11/10/9s, and Chaaaaaaaarge!!! is 140/125/110s. Kled pays no resource for any of it, so cooldowns are the only currency in the lane and the entry never quotes one.
audit.corrected: Added 11s for the hook, 13s for Violent Tendencies, and 140s at rank 1 for the ultimate.
sources: champ-data/_kits/kled.json Q, W, E, R cooldowns and zero costs

audit.whatIsWrong: The decisive interaction is absent and the page argues the opposite. It says Jousting 'gives him enough repositioning that Frozen Domain alone does not solve the matchup' and relegates Pillar of Ice to a reactive tool for his 'remount escape'. Pillar of Ice denies Jousting and Chaaaaaaaarge!!! outright.
audit.why: Riot text: Jousting — 'Kled dashes, dealing physical damage'; Chaaaaaaaarge!!! — 'Kled and Skaarl charge to a location'. Pillar of Ice 'becomes impassable terrain'. The missing-interactions file lists this exact pairing as dash-denied on both abilities. Held for his step-in rather than spent reactively, Pillar removes his entire mobility package.
audit.corrected: mid, whys[2], wants.you[2] and spikes[1] now say to hold E for the dash and state that it shuts both Jousting and the ultimate off.

audit.whatIsWrong: Violent Tendencies is never mentioned in the entry, so the reader is told to fear the hook when the hook is only the setup.
audit.why: Violent Tendencies grants massive attack speed for four attacks with the fourth dealing more damage, on 13/12/11/10/9s. That burst, not Bear Trap, is where his damage lives — and the W animation is the tell that tells you to leave.
audit.corrected: Named in mid, whys[3] and wants.foe[1] as the real damage window and the tell.

audit.whatIsWrong: The early section credits Kled with 'his passive heal from minion deaths'. Kled has no such thing — that is your King's Tribute. Kled's passive is Skaarl, the Cowardly Lizard.
audit.why: Riot text: Skaarl, the Cowardly Lizard — 'Kled rides his trusty steed, Skaarl, who takes damage for him... Kled can restore Skaarl's courage by fighting enemies.' King's Tribute — 'When an enemy unit dies near Trundle, he heals for a percent of its maximum Health.' Handing your own sustain to the enemy inverts who wins a long lane.
audit.corrected: Named King's Tribute as yours in early and whys[0].

audit.whatIsWrong: Bear Trap is treated as an unconditional pull.
audit.why: Riot text: 'Kled throws a bear trap that damages and hooks an enemy champion. If shackled for a short duration, the target takes additional physical damage and is yanked toward Kled.' The bonus damage and the yank both require the shackle to survive, so moving the moment it lands is real counterplay the page never offers.
audit.corrected: Stated in early and in the cooldown block.

edits.before: Level 1 is the one window this lane does not feel uphill — Chomp's flat bonus damage and immediate AD steal match Kled's early aggression, and his passive heal from minion deaths keeps him topped between skirmishes. Do not overstay the advantage: the moment Kled hits level 2 and Beartrap on a Rope comes up, the lane shifts. That hook is what he needs to dictate range and trade timing. Play level 1 aggressively with Chomp on every Kled step, but pull back and respect the new hook threat the second the XP bar fills — do not give him a free Beartrap on a Rope hit that sets the tone for the next four levels.
edits.after: Level 1 is the one window this lane does not feel uphill — Chomp's flat damage and AD drain match Kled's early aggression, and your own King's Tribute heals off every dying minion to keep you topped between skirmishes. Do not overstay it: the moment Kled hits level 2 and Bear Trap on a Rope arrives on an 11-second cooldown, the lane shifts. The hook is what lets him dictate range, and the yank only lands if the shackle survives, so move the instant it sticks. Play level 1 aggressively with Chomp on every Kled step, then pull back the second his XP bar fills.

edits.before: Level 1 is the only pre-hook window — Chomp's AD steal matches Kled's burst, and minion deaths are already ticking King's Tribute. Trade early and often before Beartrap on a Rope comes up.
edits.after: Level 1 is the only pre-hook window — Chomp's AD drain matches Kled's burst and King's Tribute is already ticking off minion deaths. Trade early and often, before Bear Trap on a Rope exists.

edits.before: Levels 2 through 5 are Kled's lane. His mounted form out-trades you if Beartrap on a Rope lands, and his Jousting dash gives him enough repositioning that Frozen Domain alone does not solve the matchup — he can move in and out of your W zone in ways that juggernauts cannot. The discipline here is patience: only drop Frozen Domain when Beartrap on a Rope is on cooldown, only commit to a full Q-bite pattern when he is dismounted or rooted, and use Pillar of Ice reactively to cut off his remount escape rather than trying to open with it. If you force trades outside these windows you are just absorbing Kled damage and falling further behind. At level 6 Subjugate changes the equation — drain his resists immediately when he commits, and the duel inverts. But you have to survive to 6 first, which means conceding CS under tower if needed rather than eating an all-in at level 4 with Beartrap on a Rope up.
edits.after: Levels 2 through 5 are Kled's lane. His mounted form out-trades you if Bear Trap on a Rope lands, and Jousting gives him repositioning that Frozen Domain alone does not answer. Pillar of Ice does: Jousting is a ground dash and Pillar is impassable terrain, so ice in his lane shuts the dash off outright — hold E for his step-in, never spend it on the wave. The second discipline is reading Violent Tendencies. Those four hyper-fast attacks, the fourth hardest, are where his damage actually lives, so the W animation is your cue to leave, not the hook. Commit the full Q-bite pattern only when he is dismounted or that 13-second W is spent. At level 6 Subjugate inverts the duel — drain his resists the moment he commits. But you have to reach 6, which means conceding CS under tower rather than eating a level-4 all-in.

edits.after: Full kit online for Kled, but Jousting is a ground dash and Pillar of Ice is impassable terrain — hold E for his step-in and the skirmish stops being his to pick.

notes: Disk 44.06% / 143; packet says 47.89% / 71. Riot's spelling is 'Bear Trap on a Rope' (two words) and 'Chaaaaaaaarge!!!'; the entry used 'Beartrap on a Rope' in eight fields and 'Chaaaaarge!' in two. I corrected both in every field I touched, but the remaining occurrences in fields I did not edit still carry the wrong spelling and would be worth a find-and-replace pass. The Pillar-denies-Jousting finding is the one that changes how the lane is played and it comes straight from the missing-interactions file, which lists both Jousting and Chaaaaaaaarge!!! as deniable by Pillar of Ice.
